title: MECHANICAL BACKUP

alert.trigger: No ECAM alert of its own. The last level of flight control reconfiguration: it covers a temporary total electrical loss, the temporary loss of the five fly-by-wire computers, the loss of both elevators, or the total loss of ailerons and spoilers. The PFDs show MAN PITCH TRIM ONLY in red.

effectivity.note: Applicable to ALL (FCOM DSC and FCTM).

summary: When the fly-by-wire control is lost, the aircraft is flown mechanically: pitch with the pitch trim wheel (THS), lateral with the rudder pedals. The aim is not accurate flying but a safe, stabilized attitude while the lost systems are restored. Move the trim wheel smoothly, because the THS is very powerful. Rudder makes the aircraft roll after a short delay, so apply some rudder, wait, and release early to level the wings.

items.text: PFDs show MAN PITCH TRIM ONLY in red
Objective: keep the aircraft attitude safe and stabilized, not accurate flying, to allow restoration of the lost systems
Fly the aircraft: pitch trim wheel for pitch, rudder pedals for lateral control
Use the pitch trim wheel to control pitch; apply any action smoothly — the THS effect is significant due to its large size
Mechanical THS control is available at any time if the green or yellow hydraulic system works; the trim wheel has priority over electrical control
Apply some rudder to turn and wait for the aircraft reaction — rudder induces a significant roll with a slight delay
To stabilize and level the wings, anticipate by releasing the rudder pedals
Restore the lost systems with the ECAM / QRH procedures of the failure that caused the mechanical backup
Fly, navigate, communicate in this order

background.text: Three levels of reconfiguration: alternate law, direct law, mechanical.

The purpose of the mechanical backup is to achieve all safety objectives in MMEL dispatch condition: to manage a temporary and total electrical loss, the temporary loss of five fly-by-wire computers, the loss of both elevators, or the total loss of ailerons and spoilers.
Pitch: the pilot manually applies trim to the THS; the PFDs display MAN PITCH TRIM ONLY in red. Lateral: the pilot uses the rudder pedals.
MAN PITCH TRIM ONLY is displayed on the FMA (line 3) in case of loss of L + R elevators.
The pilots can use conventional rudder pedals to control the rudder mechanically.
Pitch trim wheels: mechanical control of the THS, priority over electrical control; an action on the wheel disconnects the AP.

technique.text: The objective is not to fly the aircraft accurately, but to maintain the aircraft attitude safe and stabilized, in order to allow the restoration of lost systems.
Pitch: pitch trim wheel, applied smoothly — the THS effect is significant due to its large size.
Lateral: rudder gives a significant roll with a slight delay. Apply some rudder to turn and wait; release the pedals early to stabilize and level the wings.

gaps.text: There is no ECAM or QRH procedure titled mechanical backup in the supplied manuals; the brief uses FCOM DSC-27 and FCTM AOP-10-30-20 only.
No PDP slide covers mechanical-backup handling, and no callouts or thrust technique are given for it.
Which ECAM alerts accompany the mechanical backup depends on the causing failure (electrical, fly-by-wire computers, elevators); those procedures are not reproduced here.
